extraction.name: FLORES-101
extraction.description: An evaluation benchmark for low-resource and multilingual machine translation consisting of 3,001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia across a variety of topics and domains, professionally translated into 101 languages through a controlled translation and quality assurance process, enabling many-to-many multilingual evaluation.
extraction.creator: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc'Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzmán, Angela Fan
extraction.inLanguage: 101 languages: Afrikaans, Amharic, Arabic, Assamese, Asturian, Azerbaijani, Belarusian, Bengali, Bosnian, Bulgarian, Burmese, Catalan, Cebuano, Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, Estonian, Filipino (Tagalog), Finnish, French, Fula, Galician, Ganda, Georgian, German, Greek, Gujarati, Hausa, Hebrew, Hindi, Hungarian, Icelandic, Igbo, Indonesian, Irish, Italian, Japanese, Javanese, Kabuverdianu, Kamba, Kannada, Kazakh, Khmer, Korean, Kyrgyz, Lao, Latvian, Lingala, Lithuanian, Luo, Luxembourgish, Macedonian, Malay, Malayalam, Maltese, Maori, Marathi, Mongolian, Nepali, Northern Sotho, Norwegian, Nyanja, Occitan, Oriya, Oromo, Pashto, Persian, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil), Punjabi, Romanian, Russian, Serbian, Shona, Sindhi, Slovak, Slovenian, Somali, Sorani Kurdish, Spanish (Latin America), Swahili, Swedish, Tajik, Tamil, Telugu, Thai, Turkish, Ukrainian, Umbundu, Urdu, Uzbek, Vietnamese, Welsh, Wolof, Xhosa, Yoruba, Zulu
extraction.citeAs: Goyal, N., Gao, C., Chaudhary, V., Chen, P.-J., Wenzek, G., Ju, D., Krishnan, S., Ranzato, M., Guzmán, F., & Fan, A. (2021). The FLORES-101 Evaluation Benchmark for Low-Resource and Multilingual Machine Translation. arXiv preprint arXiv:2106.03193.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Source sentences were extracted from English Wikimedia projects (Wikinews, Wikijunior, WikiVoyage) by selecting random articles and manually choosing contiguous sentences. Sentences were then sent to professional Language Service Providers (LSPs) for translation into target languages, verified via automated quality checks, and evaluated by an independent LSP for quality assurance with iterative re-translation when needed.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: English Wikimedia sources: Wikinews (international news articles), Wikijunior (nonfiction books for children up to age 12), and WikiVoyage (travel guides and destination tips).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Articles were selected at random from each source, followed by manually selecting 3 to 5 contiguous sentences per article while avoiding short or malformed segments. Sentence selection was balanced to sample paragraphs equally from the beginning, middle, and end of articles. Sentences were checked and flagged for hyperlinked entities and associated images, and manually categorized into 10 sub-topics.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Sentences were translated by a professional translation Language Service Provider (LSP) and edited internally. Translations passed automated checks (language identification, source-copy detection, length disparity, language model fluency, and a heuristic to detect copying from commercial MT engines). Translations passing automated checks were assessed by an independent evaluation LSP which tallied errors across nine categories (grammar, punctuation, spelling, capitalization, addition/omission, mistranslation, unnatural translation, untranslated text, and register) weighted by severity (minor, major, critical) to compute a Translation Quality Score. Sets scoring below 90% were returned for re-translation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Translation quality was measured on a 0 to 100 scale based on identified error counts and severities assessed by independent human evaluators. An acceptable threshold of 90% was required for inclusion. Sets failing automated checks or scoring below thresholds underwent re-translation and subsequent human re-evaluation.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 human translation per sentence per language across 101 target languages, accompanied by human quality evaluation scoring and feedback.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Sentence selection annotators: 10 individuals (6 male, 4 female) comprising research scientists, research engineers, and program/project managers originating from East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America, and North America. Translators and quality assurance evaluators: professional translators and linguists contracted through commercial Language Service Providers across 101 languages.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: SentencePiece BLEU (spBLEU) copy-detection heuristic, language identification tools, language models for fluency checks.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dev (997 sentences) and devtest (1012 sentences) splits are publicly released for download. The test split (992 sentences) is kept unreleased and hosted via an evaluation server for shared tasks and benchmark campaigns. The authors intend to expand the number of languages covered.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Aimed at advancing research and evaluation in machine translation for low-resource languages spoken by a majority of the global population, facilitating communication and language technology access for underserved linguistic communities.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Potential translationese bias due to all source sentences originating in English and being translated into other languages, although argued to have minimal impact on low-resource MT evaluation compared to standard errors; potential copying bias from commercial translation engines, mitigated by automated spBLEU filtering heuristics; paragraph position bias mitigated by balanced sampling.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Translations originated from English text rather than natively in all 101 languages, introducing possible translationese effects. Some initially considered languages could not reach the 90% quality threshold and were excluded. Many low-resource languages lack sufficient existing bitext and monolingual resources.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing, Validation, and Fine Tuning for multilingual machine translation (especially many-to-many and low-resource MT). Also suitable for document-level translation, multimodal translation, text and document classification, language identification, and multilingual domain adaptation. The dev set is intended for hyper-parameter tuning, devtest for testing during development, and the hidden test set for formal benchmarking.
